pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care & Family Partnership - Manor Green Primary School
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care & Family Partnership
The school sees the importance in developing and strengthening family partnerships. The aim of the school is to promote a close working relationship between home and school and to foster a feeling of community throughout the school.
We offer a supportive environment for parents and carers to come into school to meet. We also offer a variety of workshops including topics such as signing and working with challenging behaviour. These will be advertised on our weekly newsletter throughout the year.
The school organises three consultation meetings in the academic year and parents/carers are expected to attend their child’s EHCP review which is held annually.
Teachers communicate with parents and carers via Class Dojo and there is a Facebook page where updates from the School are shared.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision, Safeguarding Statement and Charter - Manor Green Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision, Safeguarding Statement and Charter
Manor Green is a specialist school for children and young people with additional needs.
We provide a safe, nurturing and aspirational environment where every child is supported to achieve their full potential. Our highly personalised approach means learning is carefully tailored to each pupil’s strengths, interests and individual needs, helping them to grow in confidence, independence and resilience.
At Manor Green, we work closely with families and professionals to ensure every child receives the right support at the right time. We are proud to celebrate each child’s progress and to prepare them for the next stage of their education and life beyond school.
Many of the pupils at Manor Green have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) and a range of additional needs. These may include learning differences, communication and interaction needs, autism, physical or medical needs, and social, emotional and mental health needs.
We understand that every child is unique. Our experienced staff team provide carefully planned support, structured routines and meaningful learning opportunities so that pupils feel safe, understood and ready to learn. We focus not only on academic progress, but also on developing communication, independence, confidence and life skills that prepare our pupils for the future.
The School Vision
To support the development of a truly outstanding, creative and inclusive community at Manor Green Primary School we will:
Learn, enjoy and achieve together
Our moral purpose
"Every child is unique and will have the opportunity to succeed in their community."
Our core values:
Respect and value
Unlock potential
Inspire a love of learning
Equality and inclusion for all
Safeguarding Statement
Manor Green Primary School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. In order to ensure this, our recruitment and selection policy is in accordance with both local and national guidance.

Outreach
Outreach Support Team
We form the Outreach Team covering the North of the County, working alongside QEII and Woodlands Meed Schools as part of the West Sussex SEAOS (Specialist Education Advice and Outreach Service) offer.
As part of the Outreach provision, we provide advice and support to mainstream schools in meeting the needs of children with SEND.
Areas of Specialism
Our support includes:
Early Communication (including Intensive Interaction, AAC and creating communication-friendly environments)
Early Literacy (reading and writing)
Communication resources (including ALBs and Colourful Semantics)
Visual supports for transitions and positive behaviour
Sensory support (including sensory circuits and sensory integration strategies)
Positive behaviour approaches
How Support Is Delivered
We follow the West Sussex Outreach Model, offering flexible support through:
Email and telephone advice
School referrals will be piloted in the near future, with further information to follow.

Rights Respecting Schools
We are a Rights Respecting School and are proud to have achieved the Bronze Award.
Our Rights Respecting Schools Council is made up of children from across the school who act as Rights Respecting Ambassadors. They help make sure that every child’s rights are understood, valued and celebrated throughout our school community.
The ambassadors meet regularly to share ideas, listen to the views of their classmates, and work closely with staff to help make our school an even happier, safer and more inclusive place. They lead termly projects that promote kindness, fairness and respect, support special events throughout the school year, and remind us all that every voice matters.

pageCache.pageTitle: Homework and Remote Learning - Manor Green Primary School
pageCache.text:
Homework and Remote Learning
Homework and remote learning looks different for each year group and is designed to support learning in a manageable and meaningful way.
Across the school, we prioritise home–school reading using our reading scheme and Rocket Phonics. Reading regularly at home is extremely important as it helps children develop confidence, fluency and a love of reading, while also supporting progress across all areas of the curriculum.
To further enrich learning at home, we use online platforms such as Big Maths, Sumdog and Teach Your Monster to Read. Login details can be obtained from your child’s class teacher.
Years 1 and 2 focus primarily on home–school reading, with regular opportunities to practise phonics and early reading skills.
Years 3 and 4 continue to develop reading at home, alongside access to online learning activities to support key skills.
Years 5 and 6 are offered optional activities and projects to support learning across the curriculum and develop PSHE skills such as independence, responsibility and resilience.
Children in SATs groups will receive more formalised homework opportunities to support revision and preparation.
We value the partnership between home and school and appreciate the support families give in helping children develop positive learning habits.
For further individualised remote learning class teachers provide work via class dojo.
